facts.statement: The genus Palaeobates was first described by Meyer in 1849.
The type species for the genus Palaeobates is the extinct Psammodus angustissimus.
Three species are known in the genus: Palaeobates polaris, Palaeobates reticulatus, and Palaeobates verzilini.
facts.quote: subdivision: †Palaeobates polaris Stensiö, 1921 †P. reticulatus Duffin, 1998 †P. verzilini Nessov & Kaznyshkin, 1988

facts.statement: Palaeobates belongs to the family Acrodontidae.
Palaeobates is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Palaeobates lived during the Triassic period.
facts.quote: It lived during the Triassic period.

facts.statement: Palaeobates was a small shark reaching a length of about 1 meter.
facts.quote: It was a small shark about 1 m long.

facts.statement: Palaeobates possessed a grinding-type dentition adapted for crushing hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: Palaeobates had a grinding-type dentition, which it used to crush hard-shelled prey.

facts.statement: Analysis of dental microwear indicates that Palaeobates angustissimus was a durophagous predator that ate bivalves, gastropods, crustaceans, and echinoderms.
facts.quote: Dental microwear analysis of P. angustissimus confirms that it was a durophagous predator, eating bivalves, gastropods, crustaceans and/or echinoderms.

facts.statement: The teeth of Palaeobates exhibit orthodont histology.
facts.quote: The teeth exhibit an orthodont histology.

facts.statement: There are 33 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Palaeobates.
